messages:
sara: Quick heads-up — we need to announce a planned maintenance for the control-plane services in us-west1. Proposed window: 2026-04-12 02:00–03:00 UTC (60m). Expected impact: control-plane schema migrations + rolling config refreshes. API inference paths should remain online, but deployments, model swaps, and Dedicated capacity resizing may be delayed. I want to: 1) post to status page, 2) send customer notification (Dedicated & Private customers), 3) coordinate oncall handoff. /cc @oncall-team

sara: Link to runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ctrlplane-maint (please review edits)

mohit: Thanks. Two questions: 1) SLA impact — are we expecting any request errors or just delayed admin ops? 2) Do we want a canary region first or straight global?

sara: Good q. Expect no 5xx on inference paths — we'll keep serving, KV caches remain intact. Admin ops may return 502/503 for a few seconds during DB migrations. SLA-wise, mark as maintenance window; we shouldn't trigger SLA credits. Canary would be safer; I propose canary in us-west1-a for first 20m, then expand.

ellie: Support: can you drop a customer-facing template? We'll need subject+body for Dedicated customers, and a short push message for status page. Also a short internal blurb for Sales/CS.

sara: Draft customer email (Dedicated & Private customers):

```
Subject: Planned maintenance — control-plane updates (Apr 12, 02:00–03:00 UTC)

Hi <Customer Name>,

We will be performing scheduled maintenance on our control plane in the us-west1 region on Apr 12 from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC. During this window you may experience a delay in administrative operations such as model deploys, capacity changes, and rollout actions. Inference traffic (API requests and embeddings) is expected to remain available and unaffected.

What we recommend: avoid scheduling deploys or capacity changes during the window; if you need assistance with rollouts, reply to this email and Support will coordinate a safe plan.

We will post updates to status.redwood.ai and send a completion notice once verified.

Thanks,
Redwood Support Team
```

sara: Draft status page entry: 

```
Impact: Administrative operations (deploys, capacity changes) may be delayed in us-west1. Serving and inference requests unaffected.
Start: 2026-04-12 02:00 UTC
End: 2026-04-12 03:00 UTC (estimated)
Updates: We'll provide a start, midpoint (canary->full), and completion update here.
```

raj: Ping — we already have a node drain scheduled in us-west1 on Apr 12 01:30 UTC for infra team. That overlaps and risks compounding impacts. Can we shift to 03:00–04:00 UTC instead?

mohit: If we move later we risk hitting late-night support coverage on EMEA. Shifting to 03:00–04:00 would put rollback & follow-ups into daytime for NA. Tradeoffs either way.

moe: Oncall booking: I'm oncall Apr 12 00:00–08:00 UTC. I can own this window at 02:00–03:00. If we shift to 03:00–04:00, I'll still be oncall until 08:00 so fine. We should pick whatever reduces concurrent infra ops.

ellie: Sales asked to avoid any maintenance between 01:00–04:00 UTC on Apr 12 because of an enterprise customer demo at 03:30 UTC. They prefer 04:00–05:00 if possible.

sara: Ok options: A) Keep 02:00–03:00 (original) B) Move to 03:00–04:00 C) Move to 04:00–05:00 per Sales. Vote please (react with :one:, :two:, :three:).

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance reminder created: https://deploys.redwood.ai/maint/2050012345 (owner: sara)

mohit: Reacted with :one:. Prefer earlier to avoid kicking into post-demo window.

raj: Reacted with :two:. I'd prefer 03:00 to avoid overlapping pre-drain work.

moe: Reacted with :one: and :two:. Either is fine for oncall.

ellie: Reacted with :three:. Sales will push if we pick 03:00.

sara: Tally so far: 1s=2, 2s=2, 3s=1. I'll make a call by EOD. If nobody objects, I'll keep 02:00–03:00 since it's least disruptive to infra plan.

sara: Also drafting an internal one-pager for ops handoff (copy below). Please review: 

```
Ops handoff checklist:
- Pre-window: notify customers (email & status), take pre-backups of config, ensure canary pool pre-warmed
- Start: announce in #eng-oncall and #incidents (status update), enable canary in us-west1-a
- Mid window (t+20m): confirm canary health metrics (latency, error-rate, cpu/gpu utilization), if healthy proceed to full region
- If error-rate > 0.5% over 1m or 5xx spikes, abort and roll back changes, escalate to platform lead
- Post-window: confirm admin ops are healthy, post completion notice to status, send follow-up to customers, attach post-maint verification logs
```

moe: I'll be primary pager. Mohit you and Raj are secondary and tertiary. Assigning now: @moe primary, @mohit secondary, @raj tertiary.

statusbot: Status page incident created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rv-2050012345 (incident id: RV-2050012345)

ellie: Thanks — I'll queue the customer email to go at T-minus 72h and include the Support & Sales aliases. Can we include a short FAQ in the email? e.g., "Will inference be affected?" "How do I cancel my deploy?"

sara: Good idea. Add quick FAQ lines:
- Will inference be affected? No, production inference traffic should remain available.
- I scheduled a deploy — what now? Abort and retry post-window or contact Support to coordinate a safe rollout.

sara: Final decision: keep original window 2026-04-12 02:00–03:00 UTC. I've updated the status incident and scheduled the customer emails. Oncall: moe primary, mohit secondary, raj tertiary. Runbook link again: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ctrlplane-maint

sara: Final checklist before handoff: 
- [ ] Customer email queued (ellie)
- [ ] Status page incident live (statusbot)
- [ ] Canary pool pre-warmed (raj)
- [ ] Pre-backups completed (mohit)
- [ ] Oncall pager rotation confirmed (moe)

sara: I'll post a start message here when we begin, and a completion message after validation. Thanks all. :rocket:
